answer.summary: Pfeffer says breaking conventional rules can make you memorable and help disrupt industries by doing what incumbents do not. He illustrates this with business strategies that depart from industry norms and with investor Jason Calacanis.

sections.heading: Why rule-breaking can help
sections.content: Pfeffer gives two reasons: doing something unexpected makes you stand out and become memorable, and existing rules were mostly made by people favored by the status quo. In business, departing from those rules can disrupt an industry by differentiating a company from established players.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.content: Pfeffer points to Southwest not using hub-and-spoke, Amazon providing an exceptional level of customer service, and Whole Foods prioritizing local tastes over optimizing store costs. He also describes Jason Calacanis as defying venture-capital conventions: making many small bets rather than a few large ones, running a lean operation, and having no partners. Pfeffer presents Calacanis as an example of someone who consistently breaks rules and has power, not as proof that any one tactic guarantees success.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately attributes both reasons to Pfeffer: unexpected rule-breaking makes someone stand out and memorable, and existing rules tend to favor people already advantaged by the status quo. It usefully explains how doing things differently can disrupt industries and includes examples supported by the cited transcript. It does not claim that any requested detail is missing.
